This issue tracks the PR stack and launch contract for the GLM-5.1 NVFP4 SM120 vLLM configuration we are validating.

The goal is that someone can rebuild the same runtime state from the PRs below, install the same external runtime dependencies, and launch vLLM with the same arguments.

## Runtime Target

- Model: `lukealonso/GLM-5.1-NVFP4`
- Runtime: vLLM with the PR stack listed below
- GPUs: 8x SM120
- Tensor parallel: `8`
- Decode context parallel: `4`
- MTP draft tokens: `3`
- Rejection sampling: `probabilistic`
- KV cache dtype: `bfloat16`
- Target MoE backend: `b12x`
- Draft MoE backend: `flashinfer_cutlass`
- External `b12x` package: `0.8.3`

## PR Stack

- #39550: model-side loading for appended GLM NextN/MTP draft layers.
- #39632: MTP runtime metadata reuse and DCP-aware draft execution plumbing.
- #39633: PCIe custom-allreduce eligibility for the explicit PCIe opt-in path.
- #39634: optional SM120 `b12x` NVFP4 MoE and dense FP4 backend integration.
- #39635: FlashInfer MLA decode/runtime handling for DCP + MTP target validation.

items.title: [Feature][DSpark]: Enable varlen for GLM-5.x/DSV3.2 (Sparse MLA)
items.bodyExcerpt:
### 🚀 The feature, motivation and pitch

Adaptive verification has a firm requirement that the attention backend must not use the CPU-side query lengths as a source-of-truth, instead using the GPU tensors (so that we can run the confidence-based assignment on the GPU without synchronizing the CPU).

Additionally, kernels must be able to support decode batches where requests have different query lengths per request.

GLM-5.x models using DSV3.2-style sparse MLA should be compatible through FlashInfer's SM100 TRT-LLM sparse-MLA kernel. vLLM currently derives the sparse token-to-request mapping from CPU query boundaries, and the target capability check also includes draft attention that is captured by a separate graph manager. We should wire up the device-length path, validate correctness, evaluate performance, and merge support.

PROPOSED IN https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/52783

DEPENDS ON https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/47808

Parent tracker: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/51303

items.title: [Performance]: Tracking GLM-5.1-FP8 Triton MoE Decode Optimizations on H20
items.bodyExcerpt:
### Proposal to improve performance

## Summary

This issue tracks follow-up Triton fused MoE optimizations for GLM-5.1-FP8 on NVIDIA H20 after PR [#46189](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/46189). PR #46189 adds a Hopper `FLASH_ATTN_MLA_SPARSE` backend and already improves the attention side substantially over `origin/main`, especially for BS1 and BS8 decode-heavy shapes. **After that attention improvement, local profiling still shows meaningful decode time inside the Triton fused MoE payload, so the remaining work here is focused on MoE kernel/config/runtime improvements rather than attention.**

The planned work is intentionally split into small PRs. The first PR should add role-specific W13/W2 Triton MoE config lookup because it is the smallest correctness-preserving change. Later PRs can evaluate the more invasive W2/down TMA path and SM90 `swap_ab` FP8 dot path separately.

Environment used for the local prototype: GLM-5.1-FP8, NVIDIA H20, tensor parallel size 8, `vllm bench serve`, BS in `{1, 8, 64}`, ISL in `{512, 4096}`, OSL in `{512, 4096}`, primary metric mean TPOT ms.

## Planned MoE Optimizations

### 1. W13/W2 Role-Specific Config Selection

Motivation: The Triton fused MoE path currently selects one tuned config for both W13/gate-up projection and W2/down projection. These two invocations have different effective dimensions and resource tradeoffs, so one shared config can become a compromise. For GLM-5.1-FP8/H20 TP8 decode, W13 benefits from smaller `BLOCK_SIZE_N`, while W2 benefits from shallower staging.

Plan: Add a generic role-aware config lookup, for example `moe_op=w13` and `moe_op=w2`, while preserving fallback to existing shared config files when role-specific configs are absent. The first tuned entries can include the locally validated GLM-5.1-FP8/H20 choices, such as W13 `BLOCK_SIZE_N=64` and W2 `num_stages=2`, if maintainers agree that hardware/model-specific config data should be included with the mechanism. Some GLM-4 variants (e.g., GLM-4.7-FP8) don't generate the `<think>` start token in their output even though the chat template adds it to the prompt. This causes malformed reasoning output with only the `</think>` end tag.

This PR adds `Glm4AppendThinkReasoningParser` which prepends `<think>` to the output content, following the same pattern as `MiniMaxM2AppendThinkReasoningParser`.

```bash
vllm serve GLM-4.7-FP8 --reasoning-parser glm45_append_think

items.title: [Reasoning] Add GLM-4.7 reasoning parser for template-injected <think> tag
items.bodyExcerpt:
## Summary
- Adds a new `Glm47ReasoningParser` for GLM-4.7 models that inject `<think>` in the chat template
- Fixes #31319

### Problem
GLM-4.7 chat templates include `<think>` at the end of the prompt (after `<|assistant|>`), so the model output:
- Starts directly with thinking content (no `<think>` tag)
- Ends with `</think>` when thinking is complete

This causes the existing parser to fail to detect reasoning content.

### Solution
The new `Glm47ReasoningParser` class:
1. **Streaming**: Treats initial output as reasoning when no `<think>` token is present
2. **Non-streaming**: Prepends `<think>` to model output when `</think>` exists without `<think>`
3. Falls back to parent `Glm4MoeModelReasoningParser` for standard cases

### Usage
```bash
vllm serve <model> --reasoning-parser glm47
```

## Test plan
- [x] Ruff checks pass

[Performance][Model] Fuse GLM indexer attention projections
items.bodyExcerpt:
## Summary

Fuse two pairs of GLM-5.2 sparse-indexer projections when they consume the same activation and use compatible unquantized BF16 linear methods:

- pack indexer `wk` and `weights_proj` into the attention `fused_qkv_a_proj`
- pack indexer `wq_b` into the attention `q_b_proj`

The fusion is limited to CUDA GLM indexer layers without LoRA or MTP. The checkpoint loader continues to accept the original parameter names and handles the existing FP8-indexer-`wk` checkpoint layout by dequantizing it into the appropriate fused shard.

## Why

The indexer projections currently launch separate GEMMs beside attention projections that consume the same tensors. Packing compatible weights removes two GEMM launches per indexer layer while retaining the existing tensor-parallel layout and checkpoint format.

## Impact

This reduces decode TPOT for GLM-5.2 NVFP4 at TP4. The fusion is enabled only when both participating linears use the same unquantized method and parameter dtype; other quantization configurations keep the existing path.

Focused tests cover:

- loading a TP-sharded attention Q weight together with replicated indexer Q
- loading indexer K and score weights into the fused QKV-A projection
- routing an FP8 indexer K checkpoint through dequantization into the fused parameter
- numerical projection output from the packed weights

## Performance

Measured on Slurm node `gb200-rack1-03` with GLM-5.2 NVFP4, TP4, dummy weights, FlashInfer autotune disabled, max concurrency 1, 128 input tokens, 128 output tokens, 2 warmup requests, and 20 measured requests.

| | Baseline | Fused | Change |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Mean TPOT | 7.1569 ms | 7.0201 ms | -1.91% |
| Decode TPS (`1000 / mean TPOT`) | 139.73 | 142.45 | +1.95% |
| Completed / failed | 20 / 0 | 20 / 0 | — |
